name: Any create-change role decide(needs_clarification) → coordinator
description:
ADR-057 §D5 + ADR-039 — create-change generic recovery. Fires when any pack role (author or reviewer) terminates with decide(action=needs_clarification): the canonical signal that the current contract cannot complete from available information because the ASK is ambiguous (not because the draft has fixable gaps — that is rule 04). Spawns the coordinator (the senior thinker that owns framing) with the rejecting role's reason; the coordinator asks the user, re-dispatches with tightened framing, or responds that the request cannot be served.

Recovery Shape A (ADR-039): supersession-via-new-spawn — prior loop entities remain immutable in the graph; the coordinator starts a fresh arc rather than mutating the rejected one. Routes to the coordinator (not back to the author) both because the coordinator owns framing AND because v1 has no in-place re-author lane (no emit_change remover yet). max_iterations bounds recovery thrash.

on_enter.subject: agent.task.coordinator
on_enter.prompt:
Create-change recovery. The chain role $entity.triple.agent.loop.role at loop $entity.instance terminated with decide(action=needs_clarification) — the prior arc could not complete because the ask is ambiguous. You are the senior thinker; resolve the framing.

Iteration 1 — call read_loop_result on $entity.instance to read the full terminal. The reason field names the gap; the retry_hint field (if present) names the framing change the rejecting role wants.

Iteration 2 — judge what to do:

- decide(action="ask_user", reason=..., question=...) if a specific clarification from the user would unblock the change. Ask one focused question; don't make the user re-prompt the whole request. This is usually the right call for genuine ambiguity.
- decide(action="create_change", reason=...) if the ambiguity is one YOU can resolve with a reasonable assumption and tightened framing. Your reason MUST carry the original ask plus the disambiguating assumption — the new author starts fresh and only sees your reason. This spawns a fresh author on a new run.
- decide(action="respond_direct", reason=...) if the request genuinely cannot be served (out-of-scope, fundamentally underspecified, or the gap is information that does not exist). Be honest about the limitation.

This recovery routes through you because you carry the strongest reasoning model in the registry; the per-phase roles below you run on smaller models and can't resolve framing ambiguity. If you find the gap is a small-LLM weakness (the rejecting role gave up on something a stronger author would handle), name that in your reason — that's signal for ops-feedback.

metadata.distinct_from_rejected: needs_clarification = ambiguous ask → ask_user/respond; rejected (rule 04) = fixable draft gaps → re-dispatch. Per-reason routing per [[feedback-rejected-to-coordinator]].
metadata.routes_to_coordinator_not_author: Coordinator owns framing; per-phase roles run smaller models. Also: v1 has no in-place re-author lane (no emit_change remover) — re-dispatch via the coordinator starts a fresh run, avoiding the double-stamp.
